source.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
source.authors: Kaiming He; Xiangyu Zhang; Shaoqing Ren; Jian Sun

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains plain and residual convolutional networks from scratch and compares training error across depths, with and without identity shortcuts, on ImageNet and CIFAR-10.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own plain-versus-residual training-error comparisons and the reported very-deep residual training error. Cited findings from prior work and results on detection/localization or test error alone are not separate rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares training classification error across plain and residual network depths. It is an original source for V3, so V3 verdict labels are suppressed. Its near-zero CIFAR-10 training error also tests the clean-label part of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: deeper plain networks exhibit training-error degradation, while residual learning eases optimization and enables gains with increased depth. At 1202 layers on CIFAR-10, training error remains below 0.1%, although test error worsens relative to 110 layers, which the authors attribute to overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: SGD from scratch with random initialization as specified by the paper; uses batch normalization and compares plain networks with identity-shortcut residual networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth changes training behavior; identity shortcuts address the degradation observed in deeper plain networks. For CIFAR-10 ResNet-110, the initial learning rate of 0.1 was too large to start converging, so training used a 0.01 warm-up.
record.problems: Exact training-error values for most networks are shown in figures rather than stated in prose; no uncertainty is reported for these training-error comparisons. The 110-layer plain network is only stated to exceed 60% error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible training-error findings were left out. Detection, localization, classification test-error, and layer-response results do not measure the training-error behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and controlled comparisons of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Special initialization of very deep plain tanh networks and normalization-free residual training with Fixup.
Comparisons between initialization schemes, activation-matched initialization effects, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability training.
Matched comparisons with and without batch normalization, higher learning-rate tolerance attributable to normalization, and Fixup.

missing.what: The ImageNet 50-, 101-, and 152-layer bottleneck ResNets are explicitly reported to avoid degradation as depth increases. Record this qualitative finding without treating their validation-error values as training errors.

record.verdict_notes: V3 receives no labels because this study is one of its original sources. Plain-network degradation supports V3's stated behavior; it is not itself a scope limitation. The residual architecture was introduced to ease optimization, not to induce the training failure being measured.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test CIFAR-10/100 label corruption or random labels, Adam, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes as framed in this version.
No two-layer teacher-student ReLU problem or student-width sweep.

Tests plain versus identity-shortcut residual networks on ImageNet and CIFAR-10, but not CIFAR-10 with a plain 110-layer model trained successfully, or the special initializations and normalization-free residual recipes named in the version.
Uses the initialization in He et al. 2015 but does not compare initialization schemes or measure their effects.
No learning-rate stability-limit or sharpness experiment.
Batch normalization is part of the training setup, but the study does not compare otherwise matched networks with and without it.

rows.subject: ResNet-110
rows.operation_detail: Training with a learning-rate warm-up, then the stated schedule, and identity shortcuts.

conditions.value: 0.01 warm-up until training error was below 80% (about 400 iterations), then 0.1

rows.note: The authors state that an initial learning rate of 0.1 is slightly too large to start converging, and use 0.01 for warm-up.
rows.check: Section 4.2 additionally states that ResNet-110 and ResNet-1202 have similar training error, bearing on V1. Include footnote 5: starting at 0.1 delays convergence for several epochs but still reaches similar accuracy; warm-up is not necessary for eventual convergence.
